audit.title: Fetch and decode Data Streams reports using the TypeScript SDK

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Sections generally open with a self-contained statement — e.g. "The `fullReport` field in the API response is the signed payload you pass directly to `VerifierProxy.verify()`." Weak spot: the intro and each "Fetch and decode…" section open with procedural steps rather than a one-line answer to "how do I fetch a report with the TS SDK?"

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong — 13 headings, 1 H1, max depth H3, 0 level skips, median 127 words/section, none over 600. Clean RAG chunk boundaries. No action needed beyond query-phrasing (see D8).

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Rich: Node 20.0, TypeScript 5.3, real feed IDs, endpoints, decoded fees/prices with 18-decimal readability conversions. Facts note "0 with units" in prose but the values carry semantic labels in the table, mitigating this.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 16 internal links well-placed (report schema, crypto streams, verification tutorial). Only 3 external, 0 to primary sources — no link to ABI-encoding spec or HMAC/authentication reference to back the security claims.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good verbatim-liftable lines in the payload and fetching sections. The decoded-attribute table is highly quotable. Could add a one-sentence definition of "Data Streams report" near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, `datePublished`/`dateModified` absent, no og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified (pass raw `<head>` for a full read), but nothing was served. No `TechArticle`/freshness signal for engines to trust.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Two full examples include imports and are copy-pasteable with expected output shown. Deductions: `echo $API_SECRET` references a variable that is never set (the var is `USER_SECRET`); explanation snippets (3 of 5 needing imports) show none; placeholder identifiers `YOUR_API_KEY`/`YOUR_USER_SECRET`.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Good setup→use→decode→verify→error-handling lifecycle. Missing symptom/error-string coverage: no headings for "401 / authentication failed", "invalid HMAC signature", or "getLatestReport returns empty".

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Mostly clean, but contains a Git conflict marker `> > > > > > > c98d3598 (draft ts-sdk-fetch)`, a "new new TypeScript file" typo, and a factual slip — the single-stream section ends "successfully fetched and decoded data for **both** streams."

audit.summary: This is a well-structured, code-heavy tutorial for the Data Streams TypeScript SDK, with complete runnable examples, a strong decoded-report reference table, and clean H2/H3 chunking. Its single biggest GEO strength is the payload/verification section, which contains crisp liftable canonical statements. Its biggest opportunities are metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates were served) and a **leftover Git merge-conflict marker in the body** (`> > > > > > > c98d3598`), which is a direct fluency/trust defect an engine may ingest verbatim. Honest verdict: solid best-effort tutorial with high per-section extractability, held back by absent machine-readability signals and a few correctness/consistency bugs.

recommendations.title: Remove the Git merge-conflict marker
recommendations.why: raw VCS artifacts signal unmaintained content and can be lifted verbatim into an answer, destroying trust/E-E-A-T.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/error-phrased troubleshooting section
recommendations.issue: no coverage of the errors devs actually query (auth/HMAC/empty response).
recommendations.change: add `## Troubleshooting` with H3s phrased as symptoms: "401 Unauthorized / authentication failed", "Invalid HMAC signature", "getLatestReport returns no data", each with the cause and fix.
recommendations.why: engines retrieve by error string; concept-titled prose loses these queries even when the fix is implied.

recommendations.title: Fix the `$API_SECRET` credential-check bug
recommendations.where: "Fetch and decode reports for multiple streams", step 3
recommendations.issue: `echo $API_SECRET` — variable never set; the SDK uses `USER_SECRET`.
recommendations.why: an agent copying this verifies the wrong variable and reports a false failure.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and last-updated
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: TypeScript`, and a canonical link.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and visible freshness raise parse-ability and citation trust; this is the lowest score on the page.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first lead to each tutorial section
recommendations.where: "Fetch and decode a report with a single stream"
recommendations.issue: section opens with `touch singleStream.ts` rather than the canonical call.
recommendations.change: open with one sentence: "Use `client.getLatestReport(feedId)` from `@chainlink/data-streams-sdk` to fetch a single stream's latest report, then `decodeReport(report.fullReport, report.feedID)` to decode it."
recommendations.why: puts the canonical SDK API in the first liftable sentence, resisting generic-fetch priors when the page is skimmed.

recommendations.title: Fix the "both streams" factual slip
recommendations.issue: "successfully fetched and decoded data for both streams."
recommendations.change: "successfully fetched and decoded data for the ETH/USD stream."
recommendations.why: prevents an inaccurate claim being synthesized into an answer about single-stream fetches.

recommendations.title: Cite primary sources for security claims
recommendations.where: "Create the client" ("Authentication with HMAC signatures") and payload section ("ABI-encoded").
recommendations.change: link "HMAC" to the authentication reference and "ABI-encoded" to the Solidity ABI spec.
recommendations.why: inline authoritative links raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Tag the untagged fence and note explanation snippets are excerpts
recommendations.where: the raw `fullReport` block; the Explanation snippets
recommendations.issue: 1 untagged block; excerpt snippets lack imports.
recommendations.change: tag the payload block (e.g. ` ```text `) and add a one-line "excerpt from the full example above" note where imports are omitted.
recommendations.why: language tagging aids agent parsing; the note prevents "missing import" false negatives.

antiPatterns: **Git merge-conflict marker left in body:** `> > > > > > > c98d3598 (draft ts-sdk-fetch)` — unmaintained-content signal.
**Factual slip:** single-stream section claims data fetched "for both streams".
No keyword stuffing, marketing fluff, or unresolved cross-references detected.
offPageNotes: Site-level: `llms.txt` is referenced at the top — good; ensure this URL is listed in it and in the sitemap.
Metadata absence (JSON-LD/canonical/dates) may be a template/serving issue affecting the whole docs section; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a definitive read.
Freshness cadence: no visible `dateModified` — a site-wide last-updated stamp would benefit all tutorial pages, not just this one.
